scope: Twentieth expansion batch: 12 controlled self-assessment/intended-change examples. Six matched predicate pairs contain two nouns, two na-adjectives and two i-adjectives. One side reports a present self-view; the other uses the same predicate with naru for a future intention. These are six examples per functional target, not three examples of every word class. Tsumori is printed throughout. Intention denial remains a separate follow-up.

sources.section: Patterns of Use: noun + no, na-adjective + na, directly attached i-adjective and plain verbs; the na-adjective example illustrates a belief about one's present condition. The Basics includes an intended future professional identity with ni naru tsumori. Self-belief, intended representation and planned action are distinct contextual uses, not all an English future intention. Failed-plan and mistaken-belief examples do not establish universal failure.

sources.publisher: The Japan Foundation, Minna no Kyozai
sources.section: Actual HTML heading Aく/ANに/Nになります, structure chart, explanations A/B and teacher notes: i-adjective ku, na-adjective ni and noun ni express the result of a change with naru. The related link was resolved from the actual BTS00086 lesson HTML, not a guessed ID. The old JLPT label is not treated as a current level assignment.

Exact 積もり/積り noun entry, sense 1 intention/plan and sense 2 belief/assumption/thought/conviction. These identify the lexical functions, not automatic naturalness of the new collocations. Tsumori itself is printed, so its spellings are not missing-span answers.

Exact 成る/為る entry read naru, change/become sense, usually written in kana. Not the separate 鳴る sound verb, 生る fruit-bearing verb or archaic attributive naru. Recognized spellings are accepted without a claim of equal frequency or preferred modern style.

Actual HTML heading つもり【積（も）り】: sense 1 prior intention and sense 2 knowingly assuming a state contrary to reality, with imagined-role examples. The latter is specifically a hypothetical use and is not adopted as a universal rule that every self-assessment must be objectively false. Simplified extraction exposed only the heading; the actual dictionary body was inspected.

Actual HTML heading くわし・い【詳しい／▽委しい／▽精しい】, sense 2 knowledgeable/well-acquainted. The spelling variants belong to the requested adjective, including its ku form, rather than being lexical synonyms. This establishes recognition, not equal frequency or preferred modern orthography. Simplified extraction returned the adjacent Nihon Kokugo Daijiten entry; the precise Daijisen heading and sense were inspected in the HTML.

Exact 詳しい/精しい/委しい entry, all read kuwashii; the knowledgeable sense has no spelling restriction. The history pair accepts these adjective spellings and their ku-form combinations with naru/成る/為る, retaining 詳しい and 詳しくなる as the model labels.

authoringNotes: All scenarios are original. Source attachment rules do not themselves establish that every invented self-assessment or goal is idiomatic; retain independent linguistic review.

The question names the exact predicate and two basic forms: noun + no versus noun + ni naru; na-adjective + na versus na-adjective + ni naru; unchanged i-adjective versus its ku form + naru. The form restriction practices attachment and the presence or absence of a change predicate, not arbitrary exclusion of lexical synonyms. Other predicative or self-belief formulations are not globally wrong.

All12 items print tsumori desu. The outer present tense therefore does not decide between a current self-view and a presently held intention about the future. The English meaning focus and form instructions are visible before answering. Options and accepted answers contain only the missing predicate span.

The six current self-views include two noun identities, two na-adjective qualities and two i-adjective qualities. Corroborating professional treatment, document checking and tournament wins balance the cooking criticism and acknowledged knowledge gaps. Self-assessment is not an independent credential, a guarantee of accuracy, or necessarily a delusion.

The intended changes use the same six predicates. Study, professional preparation, classes, a checklist and practice make the future intentions concrete; naru under tsumori does not assert that the change has occurred or guarantee success. No universal assumption that intentions only attach to easily controllable outcomes is made.

Kana and ordinary word spellings are accepted, together with the change verb's dictionary spellings naru/成る/為る. Independent review identified omitted 委しい/精しい spellings in the history pair; their knowledgeable sense was verified against the exact Daijisen and JMdict entries. Accept the unchanged adjectives and all their ku-form combinations with the supported naru spellings. Pro is normally written プロ; its hiragana reading is also accepted for this grammar task. Model answers retain normal orthography. Recognition does not promote rare spellings as equally usual.

The linked article inventory and the existing intended-meaning/plan batches were screened. These self-views are not merely three more drawings or gestures assigned an intended identity. Phrases with to omou and other expressions may describe a similar mental state outside the explicit two-pattern task. Formal predicate expansions are not unrestricted missing-span alternatives in this bounded attachment exercise.

The prior negative-intention source passages were inspected again, but denying intention versus intending not to act is not tested here. Their overlapping practical uses and different descriptions of force require a separate batch rather than forced one-answer questions.

A search summary misattributed citations and suggested Maggie Sensei and Wasabi URLs that returned404 or a transport failure. They are not evidence, nor was the cited print grammar dictionary inspected. A fetched Jepang summary is supplementary discovery only; its broad claims about negative-intention force and externally determined schedules are not adopted. The guessed Bunpro ni-naru URL also returned404; the actual JPF lesson supplies attachment evidence.

All257 previous exercise records and identities remain unchanged. The shared article gains one scoped subsection and one reference bullet; the preceding transition is updated to lead into self-assessment. The existing source-guide and prior batch records are not rewritten. One SRS identity per exercise regardless of spelling or presentation.
